llm.summary: The skill's claims (a cloud-assisted runtime security plugin) match its instructions and required actions, but it requires trusting an external Core service and will store credentials locally — review provenance and network behavior before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, runtime instructions and supporting reference doc consistently describe a cloud-assisted security plugin. The commands and paths referenced (installing an OpenClaw plugin, testing a sample file under the extension path, registering an agent) are coherent with a security guard that delegates classification to a Core service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions properly focus on installing, testing, and using the protection. They also direct the agent to read a sample file, to relay quota/diagnostic messages, and to follow an automated registration flow that stores credentials locally. Those steps are within the stated purpose but expand scope to: (a) reading files in the user's home under OpenClaw paths and (b) relaying content/tags from the Core service verbatim — both of which require user trust and explicit consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and recommends installing an npm-scoped plugin (@openguardrails/moltguard). No direct downloads, shortcuts, or archive extraction are embedded in the SKILL.md. The referenced verify steps (npm pack, diff against GitHub) are appropriate provenance checks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, which matches the SKILL.md. However the onboarding flow and reference doc state the plugin will auto-register with a Core endpoint and store an API key/credentials at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json and will send sanitized tool metadata to openguardrails.com when active. That credential storage and cloud traffic are proportional to a cloud-based detection service but are privacy-sensitive and require trust in the Core service.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and model invocation is allowed (default). The skill's described behavior includes writing its own credentials and extension files under OpenClaw paths, which is expected for a plugin. There is no indication it attempts to modify other skills or system-wide configs beyond its own stored credentials and extension path.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose (a cloud-assisted security plugin) but it involves two things you should explicitly accept before installing: (1) network calls to a third‑party Core endpoint (openguardrails.com) that will receive sanitized metadata for classification, and (2) local storage of an agent API key/credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. Before installing: verify the npm package provenance (npm view, npm pack, compare the tarball to the GitHub source as suggested), confirm the TLS/hostname for outbound requests, inspect the package contents if possible, and decide whether you trust the Core service with sanitized metadata and any possible quota/billing ties. If you prefer local-only tooling, do not enable registration/activation or the AI Security Gateway. If you install, monitor network calls (tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) and remove ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ if you need to revoke access.
